newsitem.title: UK: Morgan, Salomon cut British Steel estimates.
newsitem.headline: Morgan, Salomon cut British Steel estimates.

text.p: Morgan Stanley and Salomon Brothers said on Thursday they cut their earnings estimates for British Steel Plc, factoring in the latest surge in sterling.
The two brokerages followed downgrades earlier this week from Merrill Lynch and HSBC James Capel, marking the second round of downgrades so far this year.

Morgan Stanley analyst Tim Bennett said he reduced his 1997-98 earnings estimates for British Steel Plc by 25 percent to 195 million stg from 260 stg to reflect the exchange rate and restructuring charges.
Bennett said he maintained his "neutral" stance on the stock for now, but plans to review that, as well.
"We're going to have a harder look at it," Bennett said of his recommendation. "The question in my mind is whether British Steel can maintain a 10p dividend."

Salomon Brothers analyst Terrence Sinclair said he slashed his 1997-98 profit forecast to 95 million stg from 315 million stg to account for sterling's appreciation and restructuring provisions. He said he maintained his "hold" rating.
The shares, which have fallen by about eight percent since.March 27, were off one penny at 149p at 0911 GMT.
